items.title: Donn Andre interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 6, 2009
items.q: I really didn’t like Louis Armstrong. Now I really appreciate him, very much so.

ctx.x: No. There really wasn’t. In fact, because my introduction to it, if you will, was through the bands who were playing Dixieland and traditional jazz in the late 40s and 50s, I really didn’t pay much attention to the earlier stuff. In fact some of the records, and some of my

friends will shoot me for this, I really didn’t like Louis Armstrong. Now I really appreciate him, very much so. But there was just something that was just a little, it didn’t quite swing the way the Condon band swung. And I was more interested in the rhythm. In fact, I used to play the drums in a marching band, so I had always been interested in rhythms and drums. So that’s why I have an instrument that has a head on it.
Was the Condon band, perhaps, had some swing influence to it?
